previousRound.outcome: Both blocking findings are answered at this head and verified, not read. The app's envoy-dispatch container carries lifecycle.preStop.exec.command ["sleep","5"] with the pod's grace period raised 30 -> 35, and the README no longer claims a gapless roll. TestDispatchNetworkPolicyAdmitsOnlyTheGivenNamespaces now asserts both ingress rules in the allowedNamespaces shape, through the policyIngressRules/ingressPods split. The three minors are answered too: the front-door-recreate paragraph names the in-cluster path, and the body carries a ## Contract change census. The CI line was stale in the other direction and I corrected it myself (below).

keyFindings.description: The 35 s is coupled to cmd/dispatch/shutdown.go's stopGrace by prose alone, and the unguarded direction is the canonical one. dispatch_kube.go:299-301 and README:214-217 both assert that the two values move together; nothing enforces it where it matters. stopGrace is `const stopGrace = 30 * time.Second`, unexported, in package main of cmd/dispatch; packages/envoy/infra is a separate Go module, so the infra test mirrors the number by hand (dispatch_test.go:531, `const dispatchServerStopGrace = 30`). Lowering the pod's grace or raising the sleep fails dispatch_test.go:519/553 and the golden. Raising stopGrace fails nothing: the infra test compares against its own stale 30, and the two places an editor of stopGrace reads — the constant's own comment at shutdown.go:15-17 and packages/envoy/AGENTS.md's row — name ECS's stop timeout and the compose file's stop_grace_period and no GKE pod at all. A maintainer who raises stopGrace to 45 because ECS changed leaves the pod asking for 35 and the app SIGKILLed mid document-settlement, with a green suite. The remedy I asked for: a guard test in packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch, which is package main and can see stopGrace, reading ../../infra/gcp/testdata/dispatch-pod.golden and requiring grace - wait >= int(stopGrace/time.Second) — cross-tree test reads are already this repository's habit (internal/smoke/rdsbundle_test.go, cmd/listener/api_test.go) — plus one clause in shutdown.go:15-17 naming the GKE pod as the third runtime that grants those 30 s. Either an exported constant both sides derive from, or that guard test, is acceptable; the comment alone is not, since it is the same class as round 1's README claim.

The rewritten sentence puts the five seconds after removal from routing — "a stopping pod keeps serving for five seconds after it is removed from routing" — when the five seconds is the window removal has to propagate. The code comment the same push added states it correctly (dispatch_kube.go:290-294: the EndpointSlice controller and every node's proxy learn of a terminating pod only after the kubelet has sent it SIGTERM, and the wait holds the container open across that propagation window). As written, an operator reads the propagation window as fully covered plus five seconds of slack, and will not re-measure if propagation itself exceeds five seconds — which the same paragraph, three sentences later, correctly says is unmeasured. This is the paragraph round 1 asked to be made honest, so it is held to that standard.

35 s is a floor, not a cover: the kubelet charges the hook's elapsed time, not the literal 5, against the one terminationGracePeriodSeconds, so envoy-dispatch gets 30 s minus the CRI exec overhead where the base gave a flat 30 s. The design's own reserve absorbs it — httpDrainBeforeDocuments 11 s plus documents 14 s ends the planned sequence at 25 s, 5 s inside the envelope — and the tightest pinned case is cmd/dispatch/shutdown_test.go's 27 s lock, so the real margin is about 3 s minus that overhead. Recorded in the body's Not proven / risk; no change asked.

The two new termination tests overlap: TestDispatchAppPodKeepsServingUntilItsRemovalFromRoutingPropagates pins grace == 5 + 30 and the whole lifecycle map exactly, which subsumes TestDispatchAppPodGracePeriodCoversThePreStopWaitAndTheServersShutdown's grace >= wait + 30, and toInt exists only to serve the second. The inequality test earns its place only once it compares against the real stopGrace rather than the local mirror, which is the first finding's remedy; batched with the fast-follow rather than asked for here.

thermonuclear.head: c4568c00d87d6d9fabb5d161ade829d88f640064
thermonuclear.deepReview: No blocking correctness or security defect in the round-2 delta. Answered in full: /bin/sleep is on the runtime image (Dockerfile:91, debian:bookworm-slim, world-executable, runs as the non-root envoy user); a failed hook is a FailedPreStopHook Warning event followed immediately by SIGTERM, which loses the window but fails nothing, and this repository has no monitor for that event; the arithmetic holds as an inequality and is tight as an equality; cloud-sql-proxy is a native sidecar the kubelet terminates after the regular container, so the database stays reachable for the whole drain; both new tests bite, in complementary directions; and the delta changes no rendered object beyond the app pod template. Three minors, two of which this review carries.
thermonuclear.codeQuality: No blocking defect. Its major finding is the same coupling: the 5 / 35 / 30 invariant is three unlinked literals and three prose copies, enforced only in the direction that does not matter, and it named the cheapest enforcement this repository's structure allows (a guard test in cmd/dispatch reading the infra golden, with cross-tree test reads already precedented). Also: the two termination tests overlap, and the README paragraph now carries reasoning that belongs in the code comment it duplicates.

threads: Three threads, all mine from round 1, all answered by the implementer and resolved by it as the pull request's author. I replied on each at this head with my own verdict: the policy-test fix accepted (the shape it chose is better than the one I suggested), the front-door-recreate paragraph accepted against the code rather than against the reply, and the pre-stop thread accepted with one correction recorded — its reply says the hook runs "inside the unchanged 30 s grace", which was untrue at f8ec21dfc724 and is what the tester caught and 6e01eacc6cca fixed. No bot thread exists on this pull request.
